name: Granite Switch 4.1 (8B and 30B)
purpose: IBM states: a modular LLM that composes a base model, several adapters and an encoder so that one hosted endpoint can move between natural-language responses, general and specialized decisions, and speech-to-text. It is not a coding model; it is listed because the coding area met it as a small base.

lineage.how_derived: composed with granite-switch 0.1.1: activated LoRA adapters (decision, guardian-core) plus the Granite Speech 5.0 TurboCTC encoder (470M)

license.name: Apache-2.0 (card)
license.notes: Card links the Apache 2.0 text at apache.org; the repositories have no LICENSE file (checked 2026-11-19).

architecture.kind: dense transformer with composed aLoRA adapters (GraniteSwitchForCausalLM)
architecture.why_this_design: IBM states the idea: update models like software, activating adapters on demand through control tokens in the chat template so one endpoint serves chat, decisions, guardian checks and speech (30B shown; the 8B has 42 layers).

engine_support.notes: The card lists Transformers and vLLM as backends; an official 8B GGUF repo exists, llama.cpp loading was not checked.

strengths: One endpoint for chat, decisions, safety checks and 7-language speech input
weaknesses: No coding benchmark on the card
Decision index overall 51.33 (vendor, 30B): decision aLoRA only
best_for: routing and moderation next to a coder
soft.maturity: IBM Granite family, revision 4.1.1 of 2026-10-27; about 5k downloads per repo.

tona_fit.reason: Not a coder. A possible helper (guardian, routing, speech) for a later pipeline; no evidence it improves a coding worker, so it is only recorded.

open_questions: Whether the audio-transcription area should own this record. Check: the audio inbox.
llama.cpp loading of granite_switch. Check: load the official GGUF.
